result.instructions: Read-only NetBox lookups: search, devices, IPs, prefixes, VLANs, sites, racks, circuits, journals, tags, and the change-history (audit log). Use nbox_search to find an object's reference, then nbox_get to fetch it; nbox_history for what changed and nbox_journal for operator notes. Objects are also exposed as nbox://{kind}/{ref} resources (same view as nbox_get). Curated investigation prompts (IP utilization audit, cable path trace, stale-prefix sweep, object change review) are available via prompts/list. Local writes are enabled: nbox_plan_write reviews the before/after diff + confirm token, then nbox_apply_write mutates NetBox under the active profile token; forged or replayed plans are rejected.

tools.name: nbox_apply_write
tools.description: Apply a previously planned write. Pass back the MutationPlan from nbox_plan_write; its confirm_token looks up the plan this server stored at plan time and applies THAT (the plan contents you submit are not trusted — a forged or edited plan, one issued for a different actor, or a replay is rejected). Same gating as nbox_plan_write: local stdio uses --local-writes / [serve].local_writes and the active profile token; shared HTTP/OIDC uses --allow-writes, the caller's nbox:write scope, and a [serve.vault] entry for the caller's OIDC sub.

FieldChange.description:
One field in scope for the change, with its before/after values for review.
This IS the redacted, stable field diff: only the scoped fields appear, in
declaration order — never the full object, never unrelated fields
(ADR-0001 §1, §8). Values are the shaped values the operator reviews, not
raw wire JSON.

MutationPlan.description:
A validated, ready-to-review write plan (ADR-0001 §1). Built from a live
object + an intent; applied only after explicit confirmation.

changelog_message.description:
Opt-in NetBox changelog message, validated to ≤
[`CHANGELOG_MESSAGE_MAX`] characters.

confirm_token.description:
Opaque guard that the caller is applying the same scoped plan it
reviewed — NOT an authorization credential (ADR-0001 §5).

count.description:
How many resources to allocate. `1` for a single allocation (the
default — omitted from JSON so existing plans are byte-identical).
`>1` triggers N sequential POSTs at apply time. Bound into the
confirmation token so a `count=3` plan cannot be replayed as `count=5`.

errors.description:
Hard validation failures that block the write (the planner fails closed).
A plan with errors must not be applied.

expires_at.description:
When the plan expires (ISO 8601 UTC, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`). Apply
refuses past this time.

fields.description: The scoped field changes (the reviewable diff).

no_op.description: True when the patch body is empty — the current values already match.

patch.description:
The minimal REST `PATCH` body for the object fields in scope. Empty
(`{}`) when [`no_op`](Self::no_op) — applying a no-op sends no `PATCH`.

oneOf.description: A partial update (`PATCH` against the object detail endpoint).

A server-side allocation (`POST` to an allocation endpoint that hands out
the next free resource, e.g. `…/prefixes/{id}/available-ips/`). Creates a
new object; the server picks the value and guards against races.

PlanTarget.description:
Identity of the write target, captured so the plan is self-describing and
the audit event can record it without re-deriving.

display.description: A human-friendly label (NetBox `display` when present, else the ref).

endpoint.description: The REST detail endpoint patched on apply (e.g. `/api/dcim/interfaces/42/`).

profile.description: The active profile name, bound into the confirmation token.

Precondition.description:
The optimistic-concurrency precondition recorded at plan time and checked at
apply (ADR-0001 §3). An update on 4.6+ carries an `ETag` (sent as `If-Match`;
a stale object yields `412`); older releases fall back to `last_updated` plus
a normalized before-hash, checked by a read-before-write at apply time. An
allocation has no client precondition — the server endpoint is race-safe.
Exactly one variant is populated; it is folded into the confirmation token.

oneOf.description:
NetBox 4.6+ returns an `ETag` on the detail response; the apply sends
`If-Match: <etag>` and a stale object yields `412 Precondition Failed`.

Pre-4.6 fallback: the object's `last_updated` timestamp plus a
before-hash over the in-scope fields. At apply, nbox re-reads the object
and refuses if either changed — a conservative read-before-write check.

No client-side precondition. Used by `allocate`: the server allocation
endpoint (e.g. `available-ips`) is inherently race-safe — NetBox never
hands out the same resource twice — so there is no prior object to guard.

plan.description:
The `MutationPlan` returned by `nbox_plan_write`. Only its `confirm_token`
is used — to look up the plan this server issued and stored at plan time;
that stored plan is what executes. The rest of the JSON is not trusted, so
a forged or edited plan has no matching stored entry and is rejected.

FieldChange.description:
One field in scope for the change, with its before/after values for review.
This IS the redacted, stable field diff: only the scoped fields appear, in
declaration order — never the full object, never unrelated fields
(ADR-0001 §1, §8). Values are the shaped values the operator reviews, not
raw wire JSON.

oneOf.description: A partial update (`PATCH` against the object detail endpoint).

A server-side allocation (`POST` to an allocation endpoint that hands out
the next free resource, e.g. `…/prefixes/{id}/available-ips/`). Creates a
new object; the server picks the value and guards against races.

PlanTarget.description:
Identity of the write target, captured so the plan is self-describing and
the audit event can record it without re-deriving.

display.description: A human-friendly label (NetBox `display` when present, else the ref).

endpoint.description: The REST detail endpoint patched on apply (e.g. `/api/dcim/interfaces/42/`).

profile.description: The active profile name, bound into the confirmation token.

applied.description: True when the `PATCH` was sent and NetBox accepted it.

etag.description: The new `ETag` when NetBox returned one on the `PATCH` response.

fields.description: The field changes that were applied (before/after as reviewed).

message.description: The human-readable outcome line per ADR-0001 §8.

no_op.description: True when the plan was a no-op (no `PATCH` sent).

object.description:
The affected object's JSON view, when the operation produced one to return
— i.e. an `allocate` carries the **created** object (the reserved IP's
view) so scripts get its address/id/status without a follow-up read. An
`update` omits it (the field diff is the result), so existing update
receipts are byte-identical and `schema_version` stays 1.
A multi-IP allocation (`count > 1`) carries a JSON **array** of the
created IP views here; a single allocation carries the one created view.

request_id.description:
The NetBox object-change request id, when a receipt lookup finds one
(deferred in v1 — the field exists per the audit allow-list).

status.description: The HTTP status of the `PATCH` (`0` when no request was made — no-op).

tools.name: nbox_cache_clear
tools.description: Clear nbox's local read cache so the next lookups fetch fresh from NetBox. Use this after data changed in NetBox out-of-band and you need the current state before the cache TTL expires. Safe and read-only with respect to NetBox — it only drops cached copies held in this server process.

tools.name: nbox_get
tools.description: Look up a single object and its context. `kind` is one of: device, ip, prefix, vlan, site, rack, rack_group, circuit, virtual_circuit, aggregate, asn, ip_range, tenant, contact, provider, vm, vm_type, cluster, vrf, route_target, mac, interface. `ref` is the natural reference for that kind (name/slug/ID; CIDR for prefix/aggregate; address for ip; VID or name for vlan; AS number for asn; slug/name/ID for tenant; name/ID for contact; slug/name/ID for provider; name/ID for vm and cluster; slug/name/ID for rack_group and vm_type; `<device>/<name>` for interface, verbatim after the device since names may contain slashes; CID or ID for virtual_circuit). On an ambiguous reference the error lists the candidates: pass `vrf` for an ip/prefix in several VRFs, or `site`/`group` for a VLAN VID present at several sites.

oneOf.description:
IP address. Accepts both `ip` and `ip_address` — the latter is what
`nbox_search` returns as a result `kind`, so an agent can chain
search → get (and `nbox://ip_address/…`) without translating. (Search uses
`ObjectKind::IpAddress` = `"ip_address"`; every other kind already matches
between the two enums, so this is the only alias needed.)
A rack group. The `ref` is the slug, name, or numeric ID.

A virtual circuit (NetBox 4.2+). The `ref` is the CID or numeric ID. A
logical overlay between two or more device interfaces — multi-point (no
A/Z sides) and virtual (no cables), so its terminations are a flat list of
interface refs, not a cable-path diagram.

A virtual machine type (NetBox 4.6+). The `ref` is the slug, name, or
numeric ID.

A MAC address (NetBox 4.2+). Reverse-resolves a MAC to the interface(s)/
device(s) that carry it. The `ref` is the MAC string (any common form is
normalized); a non-MAC is `invalid_params`, >1 interface carrying it is
ambiguous.

An interface. The `ref` is `<device>/<name>` (e.g. `edge01/xe-0/0/1`),
verbatim after the device since names may contain slashes. Interfaces have
no single-string ref, so they aren't journalable via the `name`-only
resolver — this kind resolves the interface id from the device+name.

fields.description:
Keep only these top-level keys in the returned object (unknown keys are
silently ignored). Omit to return the full object. A token-economy lever
for agents that only need a slice of a fat view model.

group.description: Disambiguate by VLAN group (name or slug) when a VID exists in several.

kind.description: What kind of object to fetch.

ref.description:
The reference: a name/slug/ID for named objects; a CIDR for prefix and
aggregate; an address for ip; a VID or name for vlan; a start address or
ID for ip_range; the AS number for asn.

site.description:
Disambiguate by site (name or slug) when a VLAN VID exists at several
sites.

vrf.description:
Disambiguate by VRF (name, slug, or RD) when an ip/prefix exists in
several VRFs.

tools.name: nbox_get_interface
tools.description: Show one interface on a device: its config, assigned IP addresses, and the cable-path trace (what it connects to). Resolve the device by name, slug, or ID.

device.description: Device name, slug, or numeric ID.

tools.name: nbox_history
tools.description: Return the change history (system audit log: create/update/delete, who and when) for an object, newest first. Distinct from nbox_journal (operator notes): this is the system-recorded audit trail from /api/core/object-changes/. `kind` and `ref` follow nbox_get; supported kinds are device, ip, prefix, vlan, site, rack, rack_group, circuit, virtual_circuit, aggregate, asn, ip_range, tenant, contact, provider, vm, vm_type, cluster, vrf, route_target, interface (as `<device>/<name>`). Each row includes the top-level fields that changed (pre vs post); pass `diff=true` (pair with a small `limit`, e.g. 1) to include the full before/after JSON payloads per row.

`ObjectKind::IpAddress` = `"ip_address"`; every other kind already matches

diff.description:
Include the full before/after change payload on each row. The payloads
are kilobytes each, so pair with a small `limit` (e.g. 1) to inspect one
change in full; defaults to `false` (compact rows, no payloads).

kind.description: What kind of object to fetch the audit log for.

limit.description: Maximum number of entries (newest first). Defaults to 20.

HistoryRow.description:
One audit-log entry, flattened for display. Surfaces *what changed* (the
top-level field names whose values differ between `prechange_data` and
`postchange_data`) without dumping the full before/after JSON (which can be
kilobytes per row). The full before/after payloads are included only when
`diff` is requested (`nbox history --diff` / `nbox_history` with `diff=true`),
so the default list stays compact; they are omitted (not null) otherwise.

action_label.description: The human label for the action (`Created` / `Updated` / `Deleted`).

after.description:
The full post-change object state (JSON). Only populated when `diff` is
requested; absent for a `delete` (no resulting state).

before.description:
The full pre-change object state (JSON). Only populated when `diff` is
requested; absent for a `create` (no prior state).

fields_changed.description:
Top-level field names whose values changed (pre ≠ post). Empty for a
bare `create`/`delete` or when the payload is absent.

object.description: The object's human label at change time.

request_id.description: Groups changes from one atomic request (a shared UUID).

tools.description: Return recent journal entries (operator notes) for an object, newest first. `kind` and `ref` follow nbox_get; supported kinds are device, ip, prefix, vlan, site, rack, rack_group, circuit, virtual_circuit, aggregate, asn, ip_range, tenant, contact, provider, vm, vm_type, cluster, vrf, route_target, interface (as `<device>/<name>`).

kind.description: What kind of object the entries are attached to.

limit.description: Maximum number of entries (newest first). Defaults to 20.

JournalEntryRow.description: One journal entry, flattened for display.

tools.name: nbox_list_tags
tools.description: List the tags defined in NetBox (name, slug, color, usage count). Useful for discovering valid `tag` filter values for nbox_search.

limit.description: Maximum number of tags to list. Defaults to 200.

tools.name: nbox_next_ip
tools.description: Return the next available IP address(es) within a prefix (read-only — nothing is reserved). Pass `count` for several; `vrf` to disambiguate a prefix present in multiple VRFs.

count.description: How many available addresses to return. Defaults to 1.

vrf.description: Disambiguate the prefix by VRF (name, slug, or RD).

available.description: The available addresses or free child prefixes, as CIDR strings.

prefix.description: The prefix (CIDR) the allocation was computed from.

tools.name: nbox_next_prefix
tools.description: Return available (free) child prefixes within a prefix. With `length` (e.g. 26) returns the first free block of that size; without it, lists all free blocks. Pass `vrf` to disambiguate. Read-only — nothing is reserved.

length.description:
Desired new prefix length, e.g. 26 — returns the first free block of that
size. Omit to list all available free blocks.

prefix.description: The parent prefix (CIDR) to allocate from.

vrf.description: Disambiguate the prefix by VRF (name, slug, or RD).

available.description: The available addresses or free child prefixes, as CIDR strings.

prefix.description: The prefix (CIDR) the allocation was computed from.

tools.name: nbox_plan_write
tools.description: Plan a NetBox write operation (interface description, device status, IP/prefix/IP-range reserve, tag add/remove). Builds a MutationPlan with a before/after diff and a confirm token, without mutating. Review the plan, then call nbox_apply_write to execute. Execution is gated: local stdio servers need --local-writes / [serve].local_writes and use the active profile token; shared HTTP/OIDC servers need --allow-writes, the caller's nbox:write scope, and a [serve.vault] mapping for the caller's OIDC sub.

WriteOperation.description:
Which write operation to plan. Each variant carries the operation's
parameters — the same parameters the CLI's `--dry-run` path accepts.

oneOf.description: Set an interface's description (a `PATCH`).

description.description: The new description. Empty string clears it.

interface.description: The interface name (verbatim — names may contain slashes).

oneOf.description: Set a device's status (a `PATCH`).

device.description: The device name, slug, or ID.

status.description: The new status (validated live from NetBox's choices).

oneOf.description: Reserve the next available IP in a prefix (an `allocate` POST).

description.description: Optional description for the new IP.

dns_name.description: Optional DNS name for the new IP.

vrf.description: Optional VRF reference (name, RD, or ID) to scope the prefix.

oneOf.description: Reserve the next available child prefix (an `allocate` POST).

description.description: Optional description for the new prefix.

length.description: Request a specific child prefix length (e.g. 26 for a /26).

oneOf.description: Reserve the next available IP in an IP range (an `allocate` POST).

description.description: Optional description for the new IP.

dns_name.description: Optional DNS name for the new IP.

range.description: The IP range start address or ID.

oneOf.description: Add a tag to an object (a `PATCH` to the `tags` array).

object_ref.description: The object reference (name/slug/ID; CIDR for prefix; address for ip).

object_type.description: The object type (same kinds as `nbox_get`: device, ip, prefix, …).

tag.description: The tag to add (id, name, or slug).

oneOf.description: Remove a tag from an object (a `PATCH` to the `tags` array).

tag.description: The tag to remove (id, name, or slug).

tools.name: nbox_search
tools.description: Search across devices, sites, racks, rack groups, IP addresses, prefixes, VLANs, circuits, virtual circuits, aggregates, ASNs, IP ranges, tenants, contacts, providers, virtual machines, virtual machine types, clusters, VRFs, and route targets by free text. Returns ranked hits with kind, display name, and URL. Use this to find an object's exact reference before nbox_get. Optional filters narrow by status/site/tenant/role/tag/owner; vrf (id|rd|name) narrows IP and prefix results. Pass `fields` (e.g. ["kind","display"]) to keep only those top-level keys per hit and trim tokens.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 25.

location.description:
Filter by location (slug, name, or id). Prefixes are matched on location
scope. Mutually exclusive with site/region/site_group.

owner.description:
Filter by owner (NetBox 4.5+) — a user, by name (username). Requires a
4.5+ NetBox; on older releases the filter is silently ignored.

owner_group.description: Filter by owner group (NetBox 4.5+) — by name. See `owner`.

query.description: Free-text query (matches names, addresses, serials, descriptions, …).

region.description:
Filter by region (slug, name, or id). Prefixes are matched on region
scope. Mutually exclusive with site/site_group/location.

site.description:
Filter by site (slug, name, or id). Prefixes are matched on site scope.
Mutually exclusive with region/site_group/location.

site_group.description:
Filter by site group (slug, name, or id). Prefixes are matched on
site-group scope. Mutually exclusive with site/region/location.

vrf.description:
Filter by VRF (id, RD, or name). Applies to IP and prefix results; other
object kinds carry no VRF and are unaffected.

tools.name: nbox_status
tools.description: Show NetBox connection, active backend, versions, and a token-validity preflight (the authenticated user). Use to confirm reachability and a valid token before other lookups.

ApiRouting.description: Configured-vs-effective backend routing for every surface (`status.api`).

AuthCheck.description:
The outcome of a credential preflight ([`NetBoxClient::authentication_check`]).
Surfaced as the `token` field of `nbox status` / MCP `nbox_status`, giving an
operator/agent an unambiguous "is this token valid?" answer.

oneOf.description: The token authenticated; carries the identity it resolved to.

display.description:
The user's display name (`username`, or `"username (full name)"`),
when NetBox reports one distinct from the username.

oneOf.description: The token was rejected (HTTP 401/403). Carries the server's reason.

The preflight couldn't run: the endpoint is absent (NetBox < 4.5) or
errored for a non-auth reason. The token is left unverified, not guessed.

BackendPreference.description:
Which NetBox read backend a profile should prefer.

REST remains the default and full-coverage backend. GraphQL is opt-in and may
fall back to REST for operations NetBox does not expose through GraphQL.

error.description: Probe error, when GraphQL was probed but unavailable.

probed.description:
Whether this report attempted GraphQL introspection (only when a surface
prefers GraphQL — a pure-REST profile keeps `status` cheap).

surfaces.description: Per-surface GraphQL support, when the probe succeeded.

NetBoxCapabilities.description: Capabilities for the currently connected NetBox instance/profile.

graphql.description: GraphQL capability summary. Probed only when a surface prefers GraphQL.

RestCapabilities.description: REST behavior nbox treats as foundational.

available.description: REST is always the canonical backend and remains available after status succeeds.

exclude_config_context.description: Whether device/VM list calls exclude config context by default.

page_size.description: Effective page size after profile clamping.

SurfaceRouting.description:
One surface's routing: what was configured, what is effective, and (on a
fallback) why they differ.

effective.description: The effective backend after capability resolution (`rest`/`graphql`).

reason.description: Why the effective backend differs from the configured one, if it does.

SurfaceSupport.description:
Whether a GraphQL surface is usable, recommended, and what (if anything) the
schema is missing for it. Version is a hint; the schema probe is truth.

missing.description: Schema pieces nbox expects for full support that were not found.

recommended.description: Whether GraphQL is the recommended backend for this surface (full coverage).

supported.description: Whether nbox can run this surface over GraphQL at all.

compatible.description: Whether the reported version meets the floor.

minimum_supported.description: Minimum NetBox version this build supports.

capabilities.description: Backend/version capability summary for this connected profile.

django_version.description: The Django framework version NetBox runs on (`null` if unreported).

netbox_url.description: The NetBox base URL the server is connected to.

python_version.description: The Python runtime version NetBox runs on (`null` if unreported).

token.description:
Credential preflight (`/api/authentication-check/`, NetBox 4.5+): whether
the active profile's token authenticated, and the identity it resolved to.
`unverified` when the endpoint is absent (NetBox < 4.5) or the probe could
not run — distinct from `invalid`, which means the token was rejected.

tools.name: nbox_tagged
tools.description: List objects carrying a tag, across all kinds (NetBox 4.3+). The tag resolves by id, exact name, or exact slug. Returns each object's kind, object_type, id, display, and url, plus the resolved tag. Use this for "what has tag X"; use nbox_search with the `tag` filter to narrow a free-text search to tagged hits.

limit.description: Maximum number of tagged objects to return. Defaults to 200.

tag.description: Tag reference: numeric id, exact name (e.g. `prod:us-east`), or exact slug.

ResolvedTag.description: The resolved tag a `nbox tagged` result set is for.

TaggedObjectView.description:
One object carrying a tag, flattened from the polymorphic
[`TaggedObject`] wire row. The `kind` label and dotted `object_type` let a
human scan and an agent branch without re-parsing `display`.

display.description: The tagged object's display label (its name, or NetBox's `display`).

kind.description:
Friendly kind label nbox uses elsewhere (`device`, `ip`, `rack`, …) for
known content types; the dotted type's last segment for an unknown one
(so a cable/service still renders instead of being dropped).

object_type.description:
The dotted content type of the tagged object (`dcim.device`,
`ipam.ipaddress`, …) — structured, for agents.

results.description: Objects carrying the tag, across kinds.

tag.description: The tag these objects carry (the resolved reference).
